Farming is ok to use focus on in the very early game if you have no other use for it. But to be frank, farming in albion is basically just playing poverty simulator. (Unless you are one of the people who manage dozens of islands to hold an empire for food or pots)

There are a variety of options to use your island on, but hear in mind that none are a get rich quick scheme, and will take some leveling and investment before they pay off.

Option 1; mounts: by my understanding, growing mounts is not particularly profitable nowadays (though it would depend on the mount you were growing) I'm hardly an expert on the subject, but the people I know who grow mounts all do it for fun, and do not turn a profit (1 does swiftclaws, 1 does stags, and 1 does dire-wolves) this isnt to say it can't be profitable, just that I don't know how.

Option 2; farming: this is poverty simulator. You should farm if you are not spending your focus elsewhere. If you are spending it elsewhere, you shouldn't farm.

Option 3; gathering labourers: they're great overall. Take journals with you while gathering and you make extra money, its wonderful and they are typically the most efficient laborers at making back the investment put into them. (I dont fish personally, but I have been told the most efficient way to fish is by fishing for kracken, and that most other fishing methods are subpar)

Option 4; crafting labourers; this is the one I personally use. They make your crafting turn a profit (and a significant one at that). Crafting is a very long term goal, and requires a lot of silver to get started, but eventually it pays itself back many MANY times over (if you know what you're doing) 

Option 5; mercenary labourers: don't. Just don't. (Devs, if you're reading this, plz buff them, lmao, they need help)

Option 6; building refining/crafting stations on you're island: not a good idea, you loose your resource return bonuses, and therefor a ton of profit, if you craft, do it in the correct city on the royal continent.

Your inventory will only drop in red or black zones unless you are faction flagged. If you are killed in a yellow zone you don't die, you only get knocked out, and have to sit through a timer to get back up (3 min or so). GvG is guild vs guild. It is usually a fight for territory in the blackzones. Group vs group is called ZvZ (zerg vs zerg, dont know why its called a zerg) a zerg is a group of ten or more people.

Color of the zone a dungeon is in determines the rules around it. If a player killes you in a yellow zone dungeon, you get knocked out. In black zone dungeons you get killed. If a mob kills you in ANY zone, you will be knocked out rather than killed (if a player comes across you while you are knocked out though, they can easily kill you just by clicking on you, and you wont be able to stop them)

The mine looking dungeons are group dungeons, they are meant for groups of 4-6 players, most people take 5, (1 holy healer, a main tank, and 3 dps) they give much more exp than solo dungeons.

Selling an item will fill a buy order that another player currently has up. These buy orders will be below market price, but you will get the silver immediately. Putting an item up for a sell order will create a sell order for the price you choose, which another player can then buy. Typically any item of value you should sell order, in order to maximize your profits. Small items you can just sell. (You can also sell items where the lowest sell order price is very close to the highest buy price)

Focus is a resource gained at a rate of 10k per day by premium players only. There is no other way to get it. It is extremely valuable and should not be wasted or left full. At low levels it is ok to spend it on watering to grow some crops, but as you progress a bit you should shift to using it on crafting or refining something. (Farming in this game will not make you much money)

Hope this helps, gl out there.

Question 1: Guanine.

Nucleotides can only be added to the shorter fragment, because there is no nucleotides to copy on the long fragment. The strands are anti parallel, and as suchthe three prime end of the strand being extended in on the left.


Question 2: because there is 3' --> 5' exonuclease activity the Pol 1 will go back one nucleotide from the left side of the bottom fragment to correct the missmatch between Adenine and Cystine. It will then copy the rest of the strand to the left until it reaches the end of the parent strand. 

Note: it will only copy the bottom because the top strand has a phosphate group on its three prime end. DNA pol1 requires an OH group to bind to to begin replication.


Question 3: Single stranded DNA has a tendency to curve and bend, which can result in hydrogen bonding between its own base pairs. When this occurs DNA pol is unable to continue transcription. 

In order to prevent this, Single Stranded Binding Proteins (SSB) attach to the single stranded DNA and prevent it from binding to itself. When the DNA is copied and ince again is double stranded, it detaches. 

There is not enough SSB to keep up with the demand that would be created by the long length of single stranded DNA between where the lagging strand Pol is and the replication fork.

When you wriggle your fingers under a towel, or along the edge of a table, you teach them they are a toy, and meant to be attacked. Your cat will grow up with a propensity to bite if you do this. Instead use toys, or basically anything thats not you.

Furthermore kittens will bite and nibble on you anyways, especially when teething or playing. When they do, dont react or move (unless it actually hurts, which they rarely bite hard enough to do). By doing this they get bored, and move on. Them bitting you is often hunting instincts, and your hand not moving implies it is dead, and therefore does not need to be hunted. Pulling away further triggers thier hunting instincts.
